summary: Enumerated and attributed all 49 Double-Loading Check entries (47 in agent-system/extensions/core/index-entries.json, 2 in agent-system/extensions/memory/index-entries.json). Found load_when.commands/agents have no live runtime consumer (only validators read load_when), so the 'double-loading' the check catches is structural index redundancy, not an observed duplicate-read bug. Designed and applied a decidable criterion: an entry is redundant iff every command in commands[] is agent-routed (via the core manifest's routing_agents table or a skill's sole subagent_type line) to an agent already in the entry's own agents[]; any direct-execution command (/review, /errors, /task, /todo, /refresh, /fix-it, /learn, /distill, /literature, /project-overview, /tag, /merge, /cite) or /orchestrate (broader union reach) makes an entry legitimately dual instead. Classified 36 entries as redundant (fix: drop commands[], keep agents[]) and 13 as legitimately dual-addressed (keep both hooks, exempt by construction). Designed a mechanical re-keying of validate-context-budgets.sh's Double-Loading Check that derives the routing table live from deployed .claude/extensions/core/manifest.json and the three singleton skills' subagent_type lines (no hardcoded allowlist), promotes the redundant-count to a violation, and reports the dual/exempt count as informational only.

artifacts.summary: Full enumeration, attribution, classification criterion, per-entry classification table (36 redundant / 13 legitimate), and mechanical check re-keying design for the Double-Loading Check.

memory_candidates.content: In this repo's .claude/context/index.json, load_when.commands and load_when.agents have NO live runtime consumer -- every script touching load_when (validate-context-budgets.sh, validate-index.sh, validate-wiring.sh, check-extension-docs.sh, lint-contract-compliance.sh, install-extension.sh) is a validator/linter, not a context injector. Dispatchable agents instead carry a hand-authored 'Context References' @-list in their own .md file, which does not auto-resolve at spawn -- it is a manual Read instruction. Any future 'double-loading' or 'context injection' analysis on this index must account for this: the index is a discovery/documentation/budget-estimation artifact, not a live pipeline.

Command-to-agent routing in this repo has two tiers: /research, /plan, /implement (and -hard variants) are task-type-routed via manifest.json's routing_agents/routing_agents_hard tables; /meta, /spawn, /revise are single, unconditional, non-branching subagent_type: lines in skill-meta/skill-spawn/skill-reviser's SKILL.md (grep-derivable, no manifest entry). All other commands (/review, /errors, /task, /todo, /refresh, /fix-it, /learn, /distill, /literature, /project-overview, /tag, /merge, /cite) are direct-execution with no dispatched agent at all -- code-reviewer-agent in particular exists but is currently dormant (no skill calls it). /orchestrate's effective agent reach is the union of research+plan+implement routes, never a single agent.
